# Localization · core0.19.0

```js
import {createI18n,setDocumentI18n,createMarkdownEditor} from '@ag-design/components';
const i18n=createI18n({locale:'en',availableLocales:['en'],fallbackLocale:'en'});
const detach=setDocumentI18n(document,i18n);
const editor=createMarkdownEditor({document,i18n,markdown:'# Your content'});
container.append(editor.element);
// Tear down the owned resources: editor.dispose(); detach(); i18n.dispose();
```

RU/EN are supplied dictionaries. Russian is optional; `availableLocales:['en']` is a complete configuration. `setLocale` rejects disabled languages. `configure` atomically replaces the proposed locale configuration; removing the selected language selects an enabled fallback. Invalid dictionaries/tags/configuration leave the old state intact. Subscriber failures occur after a valid commit and do not roll it back. Host content, labels, filenames, source, Markdown and row values are not automatically translated.

New interfaces pass an explicit context. `createI18n` defaults to English. Unconfigured legacy components resolve a document provider, then the document language, retaining Russian when no language was declared for compatibility. A component's `i18n` has priority; an isolated `locale` option creates its own instance context. Pass the same context across independently bundled components. Do not assume module-global document providers cross bundle boundaries.

`messages:{en:{'common.save':'Store'},fr:{'common.save':'Enregistrer'}}` supplies flat overrides. Enable and configure the fallback explicitly. Dictionary replacement is a complete replacement, not a deep merge. Region tags match an enabled base language; enable a region tag itself when formatting needs to retain that region. Missing message keys return the key rather than choosing a disabled Russian dictionary. Named `{value}` interpolation is literal; numeric values use Intl.NumberFormat. Plural objects require `other`, optionally zero/one/two/few/many, and a finite numeric `count`. `number`, `date` and `list` delegate to Intl. Currency, unit, time zone and locale-specific business rules belong to the host.

`createI18nBindings(context)` offers explicit `text(node,key,params)` and `attribute(node,name,key,params)` bindings for new UI. Their returned removers and the group disposer release subscriptions. Only non-executable UI attributes are allowed; href, src, event handlers and script/style text targets are rejected. Bindings never parse translation markup.

The compatibility facades exported by the package root/subpaths localize declared chrome selectors of code/Markdown, Git/task history, tables/grid/dropdown, progress/loading, window toolbar, conversation/activity, tree/settings, help, breadcrumbs/skeleton/window placeholders and issue summaries. They preserve the underlying data model and refresh existing controls automatically. The observer tracks only those declared controls; it never translates the source/Markdown/body/cells subtree. These adapters are for existing controls; author new controls with explicit message keys. A literal source inventory is not permission for broad DOM translation.

Caller-authored buttons, fields, select options, tabs, menus, notices and statuses receive their labels from the host: pass `i18n.t(...)` there and update through bindings. Decorative/geometry-only controllers have no text to translate. Native popup labels are resolved at construction. Numerical data and viewport state remain host-owned; DataGrid reconfigures cached Intl formatters on context updates without changing the query or edit panel. This is not a complete RTL/AT/native qualification of every legacy component. Direction auto covers common Arabic/Hebrew/Persian/Urdu tags; set direction explicitly for script-specific cases.

System language preferences are browser-local and versioned. Available languages and fallback are validated; a storage failure applies the preference in memory and shows that persistence failed. This is not an account-wide server preference. English-only hides the unused language/fallback selects; the settings form still permits explicitly enabling another supported language. Product hosts may pass `supportedLocales:["en"]` to `createLocaleSettings` to omit Russian even from settings.
